# Adjudication Task — Chapter 516

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃516화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|목적지가 가까워질수록 몇 배로 힘들어지는 것은 인간의 본능이고, 열흘 밤낮 동안 혹사한 몸뚱어리는 더 이상 쥐어 짜낼 힘조차 남아 있지 않았다.
  6|
  7|‘아부지, 지금 갑니다.’
  8|
  9|간만의 부자 상봉을 이렇게 하게 되나. 발버둥 치던 팔다리에 힘이 빠져나가던 그 순간이었다.
 10|
 11|덥석!
 12|
 13|서서히 흐려지던 눈앞이 또렷해졌다.
 14|
 15|내 손목을 굳게 틀어쥔 누군가의 손. 물이 하도 들어가는 바람에 먹먹해진 귓가로 한 사람의 목소리가 파고들었다.
 16|
 17|“노부보다 먼저 갈 생각을 하다니. 이런 고얀 놈을 보았나.”
 18|
 19|도대체 언제 여기까지 온 걸까. 나루터로부터 거리를 순식간에 좁혀 다가온 적천강이 나를 내려다보며 웃고 있었다.
 20|
 21|비로소 그의 얼굴을 마주하자 전신의 긴장이 탁 풀렸다.
 22|
 23|“……어흐.”
 24|
 25|참았던 숨을 토해 내는 내 모습에 적천강의 웃음이 짙어졌다.
 26|
 27|“그래도 숨은 붙어 있구나.”
 28|
 29|“신기하네요. 저 아직 살아 있습니까?”
 30|
 31|“이놈 보게. 오냐, 살아 있다.”
 32|
 33|“그럼 보지만 말고 올려 주십쇼. 진짜 골로 갈 것 같은데.”
 34|
 35|“엄살하고는. 아직 백 년은 이르다.”
 36|
 37|촤아아악. 투둑.
 38|
 39|강한 힘이 내 손목을 붙잡고 그대로 들어 올렸다.
 40|
 41|퉁퉁 불어 있던 몸뚱어리에 달라붙어 있던 수초(水草)가 강물과 함께 쏟아져 내린다.
 42|
 43|“보이느냐?”
 44|
 45|“누구요, 하느님?”
 46|
 47|“너를 기다리는 사람들 말이다.”
 48|
 49|나는 기진맥진한 채 눈을 깜빡였다. 저 멀리 나루터에 구름처럼 모여든 군중과, 몇몇 익숙한 얼굴들이 빠르게 가까워지고 있었다.
 50|
 51|두 팔을 붕붕 휘두르고 있는 청풍, 눈을 동그랗게 뜬 궁기방과 혁무진. 거의 통곡하는 중인 진위경.
 52|
 53|그리고…… 조용히 이쪽을 바라보고 있는 문경.
 54|
 55|- 하남(下南)에 온 것을 환영한다.
 56|
 57|짤막한 전음을 마지막으로, 나를 끌어안은 적천강의 발이 지면에 닿았다.
 58|
 59|동시에 귓가를 파고드는 맑은 종소리가 있었다.
 60|
 61|띠링. 띠링. 띠링.
 62|
 63|
 64|
 65|- [가짜 무림인 2단계]를 성공적으로 완료했습니다!
 66|
 67|- 희귀한 업적, [일위도강一葦渡江]을 달성하셨습니다!
 68|
 69|- 놀라운 끈기와 노력을 보여 준 대가로, 그에 합당한 보상이 주어질 것입니다!
 70|
 71|- [공력]의 수발이 한층 자유로워집니다! 무공의 위력과 효율이 상승합니다!
 72|
 73|- 모든 능력치가 소폭 상승합니다!
 74|
 75|- 보너스 포인트 50을 획득했습니다!
 76|
 77|- 막대한 경험치를 획득했습니다!
 78|
 79|- 레벨 업!
 80|
 81|
 82|
 83|연이어 울리는 시스템 알림. 그리고 허공을 가득 메운 홀로그램 창.
 84|
 85|나는 레벨 업 메시지와 함께 가벼워지는 몸을 느꼈다. 동시에 파도처럼 밀려드는 졸음도.
 86|
 87|“……노야.”
 88|
 89|“응?”
 90|
 91|“저, 깨우지 마세요.”
 92|
 93|그 한마디를 마지막으로, 무거워진 눈꺼풀과 함께 찾아온 수마(睡魔)가 나를 덮쳤다.
 94|
 95|
 96|
 97|* * *
 98|
 99|
100|
101|여기가 어디지?
102|
103|눈을 뜨자마자 처음으로 든 생각이다.
104|
105|나는 천천히 눈을 깜빡이며 주위를 둘러보았다. 칠흑 같은 어둠에 잠겨 있는 사방.
106|
107|점차 어둠에 익숙해지자 비로소 이곳이 어디인지 알 수 있었다.
108|
109|‘늪.’
110|
111|그래, 이곳은 늪이다.
112|
113|인간의 것인지, 짐승의 것인지 모를 백골이 곳곳에 널려 있었고 헛구역질이 날 만큼 끔찍한 악취가 풍겼다.
114|
115|더욱 지랄 맞은 사실은, 이런 와중에도 내 몸이 제멋대로 움직이고 있다는 거다.
116|
117|철벅.
118|
119|신발조차 신지 않은 맨발이 끈적한 진흙을 밟았다. 멈추기 위해 안간힘을 써 보지만 내 몸은 이미 통제를 벗어났다.
120|
121|한 걸음, 또 한 걸음.
122|
123|몸이 서서히 늪 깊숙이 가라앉던 그때였다.
124|
125|솨아아아아.
126|
127|어디선가 불어온 바람에, 늪지대에 숲을 이루고 있던 앙상한 나무들이 몸을 떨었다.
128|
129|그리고 짙은 어둠 너머에서 정체를 알 수 없는 붉은빛이 솟구쳤다.
130|
131|‘……저건.’
132|
133|불꽃이 아니다. 그것은 차라리 누군가의 눈동자에 가까웠다.
134|
135|한 줌의 온기조차 느껴지지 않는 소름 끼치는 안광(眼光)이 나를 응시하고 있었다. 마치 올 수 있으면 와 보라는 듯이.
136|
137|흔한 영화나 소설 속 주인공이라면 안간힘을 쓰며 기어가겠지만…….
138|
139|‘니가 와, 새꺄.’
140|
141|클리셰 좆 까.
142|
143|이미 사이즈 파악을 끝낸 후다.
144|
145|척 보아하니 요즘 고생을 하도 해서 악몽을 꾸고 있는 모양인데, 굳이 장단 맞춰 줄 필요는 없지.
146|
147|평범한 사람이었다면 저 붉은 안광을 마주한 순간 오줌이 마려웠겠지만, 나는 화염신장이 마려운 사람이다.
148|
149|단지 아주 약간, 사소한 문제가 있다면……
150|
151|철벅. 철벅.
152|
153|‘아, 시벌.’
154|
155|내 의지와는 상관없이 몸은 계속해서 나아가고 있다는 점이다.
156|
157|늪 깊숙이 가라앉은 하반신으로 자맥질하듯 천천히. 그리고 꾸준하게.
158|
159|하지만 나는 알고 있었다. 계속해서 나아간다 해도 영영 닿을 수 없다는 것을.
160|
161|저 안광의 주인을 만나기도 전에 내 몸이 늪 깊숙한 곳으로 가라앉을 것이라는 사실을.
162|
163|‘그래, 빨리 끝내자.’
164|
165|그렇게 반쯤 체념한 그 순간이었다.
166|
167|콰득!
168|
169|‘흡!’
170|
171|목을 조여 오는 정체불명의 무언가.
172|
173|부릅뜬 눈동자에 매끄러운 비늘로 뒤덮인 거대한 몸뚱어리가 보인다. 낮게 쉭쉭거리는 울음소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.
174|
175|‘뱀?’
176|
177|아니, 뱀이라고 하기에는 너무 크니 구렁이라고 해야 맞겠다.
178|
179|굵은 몸뚱어리가 내 목을 시작으로 두 팔까지 칭칭 묶어 버렸다.
180|
181|‘흐읍.’
182|
183|젠장. 요즘은 꿈도 그래픽 패치를 하나. 왜 이렇게 생생해?
184|
185|썩은 진흙은 이미 목까지 차올랐고, 콧속을 파고드는 악취에 헛구역질이 절로 나온다.
186|
187|옴짝달싹하지 못하고 늪으로 가라앉던 나는 붉은 안광과 눈이 마주쳤다.
188|
189|‘……!’
190|
191|등골을 타고 솟구치는 서늘한 기운.
192|
193|순간 정신이 번쩍 들 만큼 선명한 두려움이 엄습한다. 이게, 이런 게 단순한 악몽일 리 없다.
194|
195|동시에 소름 끼치는 위화감이 나를 감쌌다.
196|
197|‘이 느낌…… 왠지 모르게 익숙해.’
198|
199|그렇다면 도대체 언제, 어디에서였을까. 기억해 내기 싫은 기억을 헤집던 내가 전신을 부르르 떤 그 순간.
200|
201|파앗!
202|
203|어디선가, 눈부시도록 환한 빛이 폭발했다.
204|
205|불길하리만치 음습한 기운을 흩뿌리던 붉은 안광이, 사방을 집어삼켰던 어둠마저 깨져 나가고 서늘한 한기가 사라진다.
206|
207|전신을 감싸는 따사로운 온기를 느끼며, 나는 눈앞까지 다가온 빛무리를 향해 손을 뻗었다.
208|
209|덥석!
210|
211|……응?
212|
213|온갖 생각이 뇌리를 스쳤다.
214|
215|빛이 왜 덥석 잡혀. 그리고 왜 이렇게 촉감이 좋아. 분명히 꿈에서 깼는데 왜 아직도 만져져.
216|
217|문질문질.
218|
219|진짜 뭐지, 이거.
220|
221|잠시 고민하던 나는 슬쩍 감았던 눈을 떴다.
222|
223|환한 빛, 아니 반질반질한 누군가의 머리가 그곳에 있었다.
224|
225|이마에는 승려들이 찍는 계인(契印)이 보였다.
226|
227|“크리링?”
228|
229|크리링, 아니 난생처음 보는 승려가 떨떠름한 표정으로 입을 열었다.
230|
231|“드디어 깨어나셨군요, 진 시주.”
232|
233|“실례지만 누구……?”
234|
235|“빈승은 정호라고 합니다.”
236|
237|정호가 누구야.
238|
239|잠깐 고민하던 나는 잔뜩 잠긴 목소리로 더듬더듬 물었다.
240|
241|“혹시 가람중학교 3학년 6반 박정호……?”
242|
243|“예?”
244|
245|“너 언제 스님 됐냐.”
246|
247|“족히 사십 년 정도…… 아니, 잠깐 제 말을 들어 주시겠습니까. 시주.”
248|
249|“어, 그러고 보니까 이 새끼. 신부 할 거라고 하더니 언제 갈아탔대. 배교자네, 배교자. 순복음교회 십자군한테 얻어맞았나 얼굴 폭삭 늙은 것 봐라. 어디 절에 취직했어?”
250|
251|간만에 만난 동창 녀석이 반쯤 체념한 표정으로 대답했다.
252|
253|“……소림에서 계율원주를 맡고 있지요.”
254|
255|“소림?”
256|
257|“예, 소림. 소림사를 말씀드린 겁니다.”
258|
259|“잠깐 있어 봐, 소림사면.”
260|
261|엇. 시벌. 뭐야 이거.
262|
263|그제야 정신이 확 든다. 황급히 고개를 흔들어 잠을 털어낸 나는 조심스럽게 입을 열었다.
264|
265|“아, 죄송합니다. 순간 잠이 덜 깨서.”
266|
267|“이해합니다.”
268|
269|전혀 이해가 안 된다는 표정으로 대답한 중년의 승려, 정호가 말을 이었다.
270|
271|“이제 그만 빈승의 머리에서 손을 좀 떼 주시겠습니까. 아까부터 계속 만지고 계시는데…….”
272|
273|“어이쿠. 죄송합니다.”
274|
275|“괜찮습니다.”
276|
277|이 양반, 표정이랑 말이 전혀 매치가 안 된다.
278|
279|마음 같아선 한소리 하고 싶은데, 그래도 받은 도움이 있어서 참는다는 기색이 역력했다.
280|
281|‘그런데 왜 눈 뜨자마자 소림사 계율원주가 옆에 있지.’
282|
283|그제야 이상함을 느낀 나는 주위를 둘러보며 상황을 파악했다.
284|
285|한 번에 열 명도 묵을 수 있을 만큼 큰 방. 반쯤 열린 창밖으로 스며들어온 햇빛이 정호의 이마를 받아 번쩍거리고, 익숙한 얼굴들은…… 바로 내 주위에 널려 있다.
286|
287|‘꿈은 꿈인데, 절반은 현실이었구만.’
288|
289|어쩐지 꿈이라고 하기에는 너무 생생하다고 했다.
290|
291|한숨을 푹 내쉰 나는 가장 먼저 발치에 웅크린 채 잠들어 있는 덩어리를 걷어찼다.
292|
293|퍽!
294|
295|“핫. 오늘 점심은 고기만두!”
296|
297|“…….”
298|
299|아니, 저 기상 구호 뭔데.
300|
301|갑작스러운 충격으로 벌떡 일어난 청풍이 졸린 눈으로 입을 열었다.
302|
303|“아, 은인. 안녕히 주무셨어요?”
304|
305|“주무시긴 했는데, 안녕하진 못했어.”
306|
307|“왜요? 그럼 더 주무세요.”
308|
309|“……장난해? 헛소리 그만하고 이놈이나 얼른 떼어 내.”
310|
311|“앗, 미미야! 이리 와!”
312|
313|뒤늦게 내 목을 휘감고 있는 애완 뱀을 발견한 청풍이 외치자, 두꺼운 몸통이 스르륵 가슴을 타고 내려간다.
314|
315|아니, 잠깐. 두꺼운 몸통?
316|
317|나는 흡사 구렁이가 되어있는 천년독각사의 모습에 입을 딱 벌렸다.
318|
319|“청 소협. 그놈 원래 그렇게 컸었어?”
320|
321|“아뇨. 요즘 부쩍 자랐어요. 한창 클 때잖아요.”
322|
323|“몇 살인데.”
324|
325|“당씨 할아버지 말씀으로는 아직 백 살도 안 됐대요.”
326|
327|“……어, 그래.”
328|
329|“이러다가 저보다 커질지도 몰라요. 아, 나도 빨리 더 커야 하는데.”
330|
331|“이미 다 컸어. 기다려 봤자 더 안 자라.”
332|
333|“아니에요. 미미도 나이 먹을수록 더 커지는걸요. 저도 계속 자랄 거예요.”
334|
335|“……?”
336|
337|그럼 시바, 적천강이나 문경은 키가 최소 삼 장은 넘어야 하는 거 아니냐.
338|
339|착잡하게 청풍을 바라보던 나는 설득을 포기했다. 대신 바로 옆에서 끔찍한 악취를 풍기고 있는 주둥이를 후려쳤다.
340|
341|빡!

[P55]
*You come here, asshole.*

[P56]
*Fuck the cliché.*

[P57]
I’d already sized up the situation. After everything I’d been through lately, I was apparently having a nightmare. I didn’t need to play along.

[P58]

[P59]
There was just one tiny problem…

[P60]
*Splosh. Splosh.*

[P61]
*Ah, fuck.*

[P62]
My body kept moving forward whether I wanted it to or not.

[P63]
Slowly, steadily, as though trying to swim with my lower half sunk deep in the swamp.

[P64]
But I knew I’d never reach those eyes. I would sink out of sight before I met whatever they belonged to.

[P65]
*Fine. Let’s get this over with.*

[P66]
I’d almost resigned myself to it when—

[P67]
*Crack!*

[P68]
*Gasp!*

[P69]
Something tightened around my neck.

[P70]
My eyes flew wide. A huge body covered in smooth scales filled my vision, and a low hiss sounded in my ears.

[P71]
*A snake?*

[P72]
No, it was too big to call a snake. A python was more like it.

[P73]
Its thick body coiled around my neck, then bound both my arms.

[P74]
*Hngh.*

[P75]
Damn it. Had dreams gotten a graphics patch? Why was this so vivid?

[P76]
The rotten mud had reached my neck. The stench in my nostrils made me gag.

[P77]
Unable to move, I sank farther into the swamp—and met that red gaze.

[P78]
*…!*

[P79]
A chill shot up my spine.

[P80]
Fear struck so sharply that it jolted me awake within the dream. This couldn’t be an ordinary nightmare.

[P81]
At the same time, an eerie sense of familiarity came over me.

[P82]
*This feeling… Why do I know it?*

[P83]
When had I felt it? Where? I searched through memories I didn’t want to revisit, and my whole body began to tremble.

[P84]
*Flash!*

[P85]
A blinding light burst forth from somewhere.

[P86]
The red gaze and the ominous, clammy presence around it broke apart. So did the darkness that had swallowed everything. The chill vanished.

[P87]
Warmth wrapped around my body. I reached toward the light now right in front of me.

[P88]
*Grab!*

[P89]
…Huh?

[P90]
Thoughts raced through my head.

[P91]
How had I grabbed light? Why did it feel so nice? I was definitely awake now, so why could I still feel it?

[P92]
*Rub, rub.*

[P93]
What the hell was this?

[P94]
After a moment, I opened my eyes.

[P95]
The bright light was someone’s smooth, shiny head.

[P96]
A Buddhist precept seal marked his forehead.

[P97]
“Krillin?”

[P98]

[P99]
“You have finally awakened, Benefactor Jin.”

[P100]
“Excuse me, but who…?”

[P101]
“This humble monk is Jung Ho.”

[P102]
Who was Jung Ho?

[P103]
I thought for a moment, then asked in a hoarse, halting voice, “Park Jung Ho from Class 6 in our third year at Garam Middle School…?”

[P104]
“Pardon?”

[P105]
“When did you become a monk?”

[P106]
“A good forty years ago… No, wait. Could you please listen to me, Benefactor?”

[P107]
“Oh, right, you bastard. Didn’t you say you were going to become a priest? When did you switch? Apostate. Apostate. Did the Full Gospel Church Crusaders beat you up? Look how much your face has aged. Which temple hired you?”

[P108]
My old classmate answered with a half-resigned expression.

[P109]
“…I am the Discipline Hall Master at Shaolin.”

[P110]
“Shaolin?”

[P111]
“Yes. Shaolin Temple.”

[P112]
“Wait. If you’re at Shaolin Temple…”

[P113]
Oh. Fuck. What?

[P114]
My head finally cleared. I hurriedly shook off the last of my sleep and spoke more carefully.

[P115]
“Ah, I’m sorry. I wasn’t fully awake.”

[P116]
“I understand.”

[P117]
Jung Ho, the middle-aged monk, looked as though he understood nothing of the sort.

[P118]
“Could you take your hand off my head now? You’ve been touching it this whole time…”

[P119]
“Whoops. Sorry.”

[P120]
“It’s all right.”

[P121]
His expression said otherwise. He plainly wanted to give me a piece of his mind, but he seemed to be holding back because of the help I’d given him.

[P122]
*Why was Shaolin’s Discipline Hall Master beside me when I woke up, anyway?*

[P123]
Only then did it strike me as strange. I looked around to get my bearings.

[P124]
The room was big enough to sleep ten people. Sunlight came through a half-open window and gleamed off Jung Ho’s forehead. As for the familiar faces…

[P125]
They were sprawled all around me.

[P126]
*So it was a dream, but half of it was real.*

[P127]
No wonder it had felt so vivid.

[P128]
I sighed and kicked the lump curled up asleep at my feet.

[P129]
*Thump!*

[P130]
“Ah! Meat dumplings for lunch today!”

[P131]
“…”

[P132]
What kind of wake-up cry was that?

[P133]
Cheongpung sprang up and blinked at me through sleepy eyes.

[P134]
“Ah, Benefactor. Did you sleep well?”

[P135]
“I slept. I wouldn’t call it well.”

[P136]
“Why not? Then sleep some more.”

[P137]
“…Are you kidding me? Stop talking nonsense and get this thing off me.”

[P138]
“Oh! Mimi! Come here!”

[P139]
Cheongpung finally noticed the pet snake coiled around my neck. At his call, its thick body slid down across my chest.

[P140]
Wait. *Thick?*

[P141]
I stared at the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake. It looked practically like a python now.

[P142]
“Young Hero Cheongpung. Was it always that big?”

[P143]
“No. It’s grown a lot lately. It’s at that age.”

[P144]
“How old is it?”

[P145]
“Grandpa Tang says it isn’t even a hundred yet.”

[P146]
“…Oh. I see.”

[P147]
“It might get bigger than me. Ah, I need to hurry up and grow more too.”

[P148]
“You’re already grown. Waiting won’t make you any taller.”

[P149]
“No, I’m not. Mimi keeps getting bigger as she gets older. I’ll keep growing too.”

[P150]
“…?”

[P151]
Then shouldn’t Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong be at least three zhang tall by now?

[P152]
I gave Cheongpung a troubled look and gave up trying to convince him. Instead, I smacked the mouth beside me that was giving off a horrific stench.

[P153]
*Smack!*

[P154]
“Urgh!”

[P155]
“I told you to brush your teeth before bed. You damn beggar, your mouth’s a swamp. A fucking swamp.”

[P156]
“Guh. Guhhh.”

[P157]
Gung Gibang woke up and glared at me, his eyes watering.

[P158]
“Why do you always pick on me?”

[P159]
“I don’t pick on *only* you. I’m going to deal with this guy the same way.”

[P160]
People ought to be treated equally.

[P161]
A moment later, Hyuk Mujin, who had been sleeping soundly with one of my legs clutched in his arms, met the same fate.

[P162]
*Whack!*

[P163]
“Argh! Why do you always pick on me?”

[P164]
“Did you two rehearse that? Or are you brothers separated when you were little?”

[P165]
“Don’t just hit me. Young Hero Gung too—oh, he’s awake.”

[P166]
“…Hah. You hateful bastards.”

[P167]
I gave the muttering Hyuk Mujin a kick that sent him tumbling off the bed.

[P168]
Because of these idiots, I’d had a dream when I hardly ever dreamed at all. And it had been an unsettling nightmare.

[P169]
*That gaze.*

[P170]
The red light still sent a chill through me. I was trying to recall that strange feeling from the dream when Jung Ho, who had slipped out during the commotion, came back through the door.

[P171]
“Benefactor Jin. Could you spare me a moment?”

[P172]
“Ah, yes.”

[P173]
I sat up straight. After rubbing his head like a bowling ball, I’d have had to make time for him even if I didn’t have any.

[P174]
“Please, speak, Monk.”

[P175]
“My Martial Uncle wishes to see you, Benefactor.”

[P176]
“Your Martial Uncle? Is he the person waiting outside?”

[P177]
“Yes. He says he would like to speak with you again after so long…”

[P178]
So that was it. I’d wondered why I could sense two presences.

[P179]
Jung Ho’s Martial Uncle had to be a senior monk of Shaolin. But someone who wanted to speak with me *again*?

[P180]
*Who is it? The way he put it, we’ve definitely met before.*

[P181]
Besides the Dharma King, had I grown that close to anyone else at Shaolin?

[P182]
I nodded readily enough.

[P183]
“Of course.”

[P184]
No sooner had I spoken than someone came through the door. I frowned.

[P185]
“Excuse me, but who…?”

[P186]
The monk was slender, with scars covering every bit of exposed skin. He had a fierce look about him, and his voice was rough.

[P187]
“I’m glad. Though the heavens have grown dim, the Morning Star that rose in the north seems to shine even brighter.”

[P188]
“…!”

[P189]
“How have you been, Benefactor?”

[P190]
Only then did I recognize the monk before me. His appearance and the air about him had changed so much that it had taken me a moment to find his name.

[P191]
“Unnamed.”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
